rule_or_pattern: On this book's two-column pages drop every line whose crop is wider than 0.55 x the text width (not only >0.8), plus all lines flagged C:cpp_vs_book_out, C:len_vs_book_high or C:cph_out_of_range. If the yield after this is small, drop the whole book.
notes: This is an 1867 two-column polytonic parliament record. Google joins the two columns into one line very often: 11 of the 20 random lines (3, 5-9, 13-15, 18-20) are cross-gutter crops. In the anomalous lines (21-40) the crop spans both columns while the label is a short fragment of one side ('διώρισα ἕνα', 'κατάστασιν'). The page image shows interleaved, overprinted readings. Single-column-width lines (1, 2, 4, 10, 12, 16, 17) read correctly, with good polytonic marks. Line 11, however, carries another line's text under an unflagged single-column crop, so even the survivors carry some risk.
